blurb: Once Edo, a castle town that became one of the largest cities on Earth. Its prints changed how Europe painted.

facts.t: Tokugawa Ieyasu made the small castle town of Edo his capital. His family ruled Japan from here for over 250 years, and Edo grew to about a million people. In 1868 the emperor moved in and the city was renamed Tokyo, Eastern Capital. The Imperial Palace stands on the old castle grounds.

facts.h: Hokusai was a child of Edo
facts.t: Hokusai was born in the Sumida district and moved house more than ninety times, by his own count. He made the Great Wave in his early seventies, for a print series of views of Mount Fuji. The Sumida Hokusai Museum stands near where he was born.

Hiroshige's One Hundred Famous Views of Edo showed the city's bridges, gardens and rain. Thirty years later in Paris, Van Gogh copied two of them in oil, a plum garden and a bridge in a sudden shower, and framed them with Japanese letters he did not understand.
